sections.label: Replacing DC, TDL, DP with LBC
sections.summary: This Bill proposes a single LBC to replace the DC, TDL and DP paid to URA and SLA.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Under this existing framework, landowners and developers currently have to pay a DC or a TDL to URA, where the grant of planning permission for a development proposal regarding land results in an enhancement to land value, or a DP to SLA if there is an enhancement in land value resulting from a waiver or variation of a restrictive covenant contained in the state title of that piece of land.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: This Bill proposes for a single LBC to replace the DC, the TDL and the DP.

sections.label: LBC charged by SLA
sections.summary: The LBC will be charged and collected by a single agency, SLA.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: One key change is that the LBC will be charged by and collected by a single agency – in this case, SLA.

sections.label: LBC rate at 70%
sections.summary: The LBC rate will be set at 70% of the increase in land value from consent for land development proposals.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: In general, though, I should tell Members that the LBC rate will be set at 70% of the increase in land value arising from the grant of consent for proposals involving the development of land which is what it currently is today.

sections.label: Leasehold factor for state leases
sections.summary: LBC for state leases with residual tenure of 99 years or less will be adjusted by a leasehold factor.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The LBC payable for all state leases with a residual tenure of 99 years or less will be adjusted by a leasehold factor to account for the remaining tenure of leasehold land.

sections.label: LBC liability and deferment
sections.summary: Land owners are liable for LBC by default, but others may assume or be transferred deferred liability with SLA approval.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Under the Bill, every person who is an owner of the land when a chargeable consent is given is liable to pay LBC, by default.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: However, another party other than the owner of the land can assume liability to pay the LBC if a valid assumption of liability notice is given to SLA, or if liability to pay LBC has been deferred and the deferred liability is transferred to that other party with SLA’s approval.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The Bill sets out one main set of circumstances where deferment may be allowed by SLA, which is if the taxable person is a charitable institution and where the land is used wholly or mainly for charitable purposes.

sections.label: Penalty tax at 30%
sections.summary: In that situation, the penalty tax is fixed at 30% of the LBC due.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: In that situation, the penalty tax is fixed at 30% of the LBC that is due.

sections.label: Land Betterment Charge as tax
sections.summary: The Land Betterment Charge is a tax diverting part of increased value created by the public body's decision for public good.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The Land Betterment Charge represents a tax to divert part of the increased value, created by the decision of the public body, for public good.

sections.label: DP and DC concepts consolidated
sections.summary: A DP is levied by contract on the developer for lifting title restrictions, unlike DC which is a tax, and this Bill consolidates these concepts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: A DP is levied, as a matter of contract, unlike DC which is a tax, by the Government on the developer in return for the Government lifting title restrictions that will have the effect of increasing the value of the land.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This Bill consolidates these concepts under one Bill.

sections.label: DP system outside restrictive covenants
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the DP system will continue to operate outside the lifting of restrictive covenants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: First, will the DP system continue to operate outside the lifting of restrictive covenants?

sections.label: Why not consolidate DP situation
sections.summary: The passage asks why the Government is not minded to bring such a situation under the Bill meant to consolidate DC and DP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: If my reading is correct, may I please ask: why is the Government not minded to bring such a situation under the Bill since the intent of the Bill is to consolidate the concepts of DC and DP under one single Bill?

sections.label: Three charges under single framework
sections.summary: The speaker declares interest as a research consultancy CEO and says the Bill brings three separate charges under a single Land Betterment Charge framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Before I proceed, I declare my interest as a CEO of a research consultancy that undertakes work in a broad range of fields.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This Bill brings together in streamlines three separate charges under a single Land Betterment Charge framework.

sections.label: No public consultation on charges
sections.summary: The speaker was surprised there was no public consultation or public consultation results made available on the Bill's scale of charges.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Next, given the scale of charges set forth by this Bill, I was surprised that there was no public consultation – to the best of my knowledge – and no public consultation results made available to the public or press or in the press release by the Ministry on the Bill.

sections.label: LBC use and purpose
sections.summary: The Bill aims to return economic benefits from land development to the community, but the LBC would go into Government revenues for general expenditure rather than being earmarked for community projects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The foremost purpose of this Bill is to, "ensure the return to the community" of economic benefits reaped from the development of land.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, it appears that the LBC would go into Government revenues and be consolidated with other tax revenues for their general expenditure instead of being earmarked for particular projects that benefit the community.

sections.label: Clause 13 concessionary relief
sections.summary: Clause 13 provides concessionary relief if development shows desirability in achieving economic development or maintaining the well-being of the people and community, though the broad wording warrants caution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Next, clause 13 provides for concessionary relief if the development shows "desirability in achieving economic development or maintaining the cultural, economic, physical and social well-being of the people of Singapore and the community in the area concerned." While it is understandable that this is worded in broad terms to cover a spectrum of possible developments that may fall under this, we should be wary of too broad a scope.

sections.label: Golden Mile Complex conservation incentives
sections.summary: URA proposed Golden Mile Complex for conservation and offered developers planning incentives including a one-third floor area increase and a waiver of part of its development charge.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Last October, when URA proposed the Golden Mile Complex for conservation to ensure that this move would not inhibit a future collective sale, they offered developers additional planning incentives, including a one-third increase in floor area and a waiver of a part of its development charge.

sections.label: SWF Jubilee Industrial Building TDL
sections.summary: In 2015, the Singapore Weightlifting Federation moved into Jubilee Industrial Building and had to pay estimated TDL of $34,000 a year for sports-related use.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To take one illustration, in 2015, when the Singapore Weightlifting Federation, or SWF, moved into the Jubilee Industrial Building that is slated for industrial use, they had to pay at TDL estimated at $34,000 a year to use the space for sports-related purposes.

sections.label: Stamp duty on LBC
sections.summary: The passage asks whether stamp duty will be additionally leviable on payment of LBC to the relevant authorities, since LBC is a tax under clause 7.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As the LBC is a tax, as seen in clause 7 of the Bill, will stamp duty be additionally leviable on payment of LBC to the relevant authorities?

sections.label: LBC payment under clause 24(4)
sections.summary: Under clause 24(4), LBC is payable at the end of one month after a liability order is issued by SLA unless otherwise stated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Under clause 24(4) of this Bill, however, LBC is payable at the end of one month after a liability order is issued by SLA unless otherwise stated.

sections.label: Landowner liable for LBC
sections.summary: Under the new Bill, the landowner with material interest in the land is by default liable to pay the LBC, providing clarity over previous disputes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Under the new Bill, the landowner with material interest in the land is by default liable to pay the LBC, providing clarity compared to the previous situation where landlords and tenants sometimes disputed the paying of TDL.

sections.label: Minister remitting LBC hardship
sections.summary: The Minister can decide case-by-case to remit LBC, including where a natural person liable has suffered loss or serious hardship.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Lastly, Sir, right now, the Minister is able to decide on a case-by-case basis to defy liability to pay LBC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For example, can we consider deferment due to tenants – namely small businesses – finding it difficult to pay TDL, especially those hard hit by the pandemic?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I noted that clause 14, the Minister can remit, in whole or in part, any Land Betterment Charge where the Minister is satisfied of certain conditions, including if a natural person liable to pay has suffered a loss or is in such circumstances that the charge would entail serious hardship.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To quote from the recent Budget cut speech made by my parliamentary colleague, Mr Gerald Giam, and I quote, "Some businesses have lamented to me that their TDL far exceeds business revenue, especially during the pandemic.

sections.label: Minister concessionary relief power
sections.summary: New section 13 gives the Land Planning Minister power to provide concessionary relief from LBC for certain planning objectives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The new section 13 of the Bill provides the Land Planning Minister the power to provide concessionary relief from Land Betterment Charge (LBC) for the purpose of meeting certain planning objectives.

sections.label: Minister general exemptions scope
sections.summary: The second point concerns the scope of the Minister's power to grant general exemptions from LBC under new section 12.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: My second point is on the scope of Minister's power to grant general exemptions from the Land Betterment Charge under the new section 12.

sections.label: Authority penalty tax power
sections.summary: New section 40(2)(d) lets the Authority direct payment of penalty tax if restoration is not reasonably practicable or is undesirable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The new section 40(2)(d) provides the Authority the power to direct a person to pay a penalty tax if the Authority considers that restoring the land and other restorative steps is not reasonably practicable or is undesirable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: At present, the Authority's power to either order restoration or impose a penalty tax appears to be mutually exclusive.

sections.label: Public sector land ownership
sections.summary: From 1960-2007, land owned by the public sector doubled from 44% to over 85%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The effect of legislation has meant that from 1960-2007, land owned by the public sector doubled from 44% to over 85%.

sections.label: Land Betterment Charge mechanism
sections.summary: The Land Betterment Charge is an additional mechanism to collect a tax on land value increase from a chargeable consent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The Land Betterment Charge (LBC) will be one additional mechanism, the principles of which I agree with, as it will allow for the collection of a tax on the increase in the value of land resulting from a chargeable consent given in relation to the land.

sections.label: LBC replaces DC, TDL, DP
sections.summary: The Land Betterment Charge is collected by SLA and replaces Development Charge, Temporary Development Levy and Differential Premium collection.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Specific to the Land Betterment Charge, I note that it is to be collected by SLA and replaces the taxes known as Development Charge (DC) and Temporary Development Levy (TDL) imposed under the Planning Act and the collection of Differential Premium (DP) by SLA.

sections.label: DC rates table breakdown
sections.summary: The table of DC rates is broken down into 118 geographical sectors and nine different use groups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The table of DC rates are broken down into 118 geographical sectors and nine different use groups.

sections.label: Concessionary relief from LBC
sections.summary: Clause 13 empowers the land planning Minister to provide for concessionary relief from Land Betterment Charges under certain conditions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Fourth, clause 13 empowers the land planning Minister to provide for concessionary relief from Land Betterment Charges, assuming certain conditions have been made.

sections.label: Lessee or occupier liability
sections.summary: Under clause 35, if the taxable person defaults on LBC payment, the lessee or occupier is liable for payment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Fifth, on the liability of lessees or occupiers, under clause 35, should the taxable person make default in payment of any LBC, the lessee or occupier will be liable for payment, notwithstanding that any such payments constitute a valid discharge from rents or payments due.

sections.label: Purpose of LBC and land revenue
sections.summary: The speaker agrees with the LBC's purpose and notes land sales revenue is not in the Government's operating Budget.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: To round up, Mr Speaker, I agree with the purpose of the LBC and recognise it is one of the many ways in which land in Singapore can be continuously monetised by the Government to provide for recurring revenue throughout the course of time; although I recognise at this point in time, the Government does not take into its operating Budget the recurring annual land sales revenue of about $14.5 billion on average.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: With Singapore's Budget not inclusive of land sales revenue, it is worth considering realigning the focus in the sale of state land from one of revenue maximisation in that land is awarded to the highest bidder to one in which the greatest value uplift can be provided and the greatest socioeconomic good generated, similar to that as encouraged by the LBC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The LBC will replace the current Differential Premium (DP), Development Charge (DC) or Temporary Development Levy (TDL) payments.

sections.label: Sharing economic benefits with community
sections.summary: Clause 5 states the first objective is to ensure a fair proportion of expected economic benefits from land development is shared with the community.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The first objective, as stated in clause 5, is to ensure that a fair proportion of the expected economic benefits from the land development is shared with the community.

sections.label: Certainty and transparency in charges
sections.summary: The second aim is to provide certainty and transparency through rules and processes for calculating most land betterment charges by reference to fixed data without valuation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The second aim is to provide, I quote, "certainty and transparency through rules and processes for calculating most land betterment charges by reference to fixed data without need for valuation".

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Presently, under URA, DC rates are reviewed every six months in March and September in consultation with the Chief Valuer at IRAS.

sections.label: Continuation of existing DC reliefs
sections.summary: Section 13 provisions enable the continuation of existing concessionary reliefs from Development Charge currently provided for in the Planning Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The provisions in section 13 enable the continuation of existing concessionary reliefs from Development Charge (DC), currently provided for in the Planning Act.

sections.label: LBC collections into Consolidated Fund
sections.summary: Clause 57 of the Bill requires all LBC collections to be paid into the Consolidated Fund.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Clause 57 in the Bill requires all LBC collections to be paid into the Consolidated Fund.

sections.label: Penalty tax for unlawful developments
sections.summary: No penalty tax is provided for unlawful developments where no consent is granted, but a penalty of up to 30% may be levied when permission is later granted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: It does not provide for a penalty tax to be collected for unlawful developments where no such consent is granted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, if you have something that is done in breach of the restrictive covenants, for example, then, subsequently when the permission is granted, not only will LBC be collected, there will also be a penalty amount levied on top of that; up to 30%, as I mentioned at the outset.

sections.label: LBC liability and chargeable consent
sections.summary: LBC is not a tax to cream off transactions that appreciate land value; liability arises only when the state grants a chargeable consent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And I hope that clarifies Mr Murali's point.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: I should clarify to this House that the LBC is not a tax to cream-off any transaction that leads to an appreciation land value.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The liability to pay LBC arises only when the state grants a chargeable consent by allowing a landowner to develop the land further or varying a restrictive covenant in the state title, so that you can do something, which you previously could not do under the title.

sections.label: Stamp duty on LBC
sections.summary: Stamp duty is not leviable on the LBC because the LBC is a tax, as Mr Perera pointed out.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Stamp duty is not leviable on the LBC, as the LBC is a tax, as Mr Perera had pointed out.

sections.label: Timing of LBC and DP payment
sections.summary: Both the LBC and the DP are generally payable after PP but before the Written Permission.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: As to timing of the payment raised by Mr Perera, both the LBC and the DP are generally payable after PP, but before the Written Permission.
